definition: Morose means sunk in gloom that has settled in and pushes company away.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word morose. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know morose should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: After the bakery turned down his sourdough, Amos was morose for a week, kneading in silence and glaring at the proofing loaves.
Glum is milder than morose — a passing afternoon of low spirits, while a morose mood sinks into gloom that settles in and turns sullen enough to push company away.
Despairing goes further than morose — beyond gloom into the conviction that nothing will ever improve.

Sullen is silent resentment: the slammed door, the one-word answers aimed at whoever caused the mood. Morose shares the gloom but drops the grudge — a morose person is sunk in darkness that has settled in for weeks, not punishing anyone in particular.

Melancholy means gently, thoughtfully sad — wistful autumn evenings, old letters, a mood a person can almost enjoy. Morose strips away that sweetness: the gloom turns heavy and unsociable, with a sullen edge that pushes company away rather than inviting quiet reflection.
